Because of the wonderful snowman, er, I mean, checkmark, shouldn't we always be getting UTF-8 encoded data?

I guess someone can send something else through CURL.

> Because of the wonderful snowman, er, I mean, checkmark, shouldn't we always be getting UTF-8 encoded data?

Unfortunately no. I'm talking about data that does not come from a form. I'm talking about data like HTTP_REFERER, PATH_INFO and other data available in `request.env`. I doesn't matter if we're getting UTF-8 or not since the strings are tagged as binary/ascii and IE doesn't do any CGI escaping.
Ahh, yes. That's what I get for commenting right before bedtime. :)
By digging through the Rails code I found another function that can be used to escape URI's, `URI.parser.escape`. This would solve the problem the `CGI.escape` function is causing.

I have the same problem with Rails 3.2.13 and IE10 on a search form result page followed by a product show page which contains a `link_to "Back", :back` link. Because of the `utf8=✓` in the referer, I got an `incompatible character encodings: ASCII-8BIT and UTF-8` exception.

Just realised, that it only happens, when I copy&paste the search result link into the browser (what may happen when someone send the link to a friend e.g. per mail). When the form get submitted as usual in IE8 and IE10, the `utf8=✓` becomes `utf8=%E2%9C%93`.

I think I was able to reproduce this without copy pasting. Like using a search form and searching for something outside the ascii table. If I do the same search twice `request.evn["HTTP_REFERER"]` will contain unescaped UTF-8 characters that are tagged as ascii/binary.

On my app a search for "bäume" results in `/produkte/suche?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=b%C3%A4ume` no matter how often I submit it. Tested with IE8 (XP) and IE10 (Win8). I think the browser escape the characters because the requests against the server come in escaped and so the referer is also escaped. I use the HTML5 Doctype an `<meta charset="utf-8">`. Rails also add `accept-charset="UTF-8"` to the form tag. I´m sorry but I only can confirm the issue when I copy and paste the unescaped URL.
Hmm, I'll take a look at how to exactly reproduce the error. What about if you the second time just press enter in the address field in the browser to repeat the request?
Since my form is submitted per GET, this is not a problem.

> Since my form is submitted per GET, this is not a problem.

I think that is where the problem is. The URL will contain the parameters from the form, i.e. UTF-8. This is what will end up in `request.evn["HTTP_REFERER"]` and other environment variables but IE doesn't URL encode that data. Since all strings in `request.env` is tagged as binary you'll get an exception when manipulating the string.

This is my results from testing. I've used the search form on our website and search for "kök" which includes a UTF-8 character outside the ASCII table. The search request is a GET request. I've added a middleware that is placed just after `Rack::Lock` and printed data from the environment that is passed in.

IE6:

The actual request: "REQUEST_URI"=>"/se/sok?q=k\xC3\xB6k"
The first image that is requested: "HTTP_REFERER"=>"http://10.180.12.113:3000/se/sok?q=k\xF6k"

IE9 and IE10 (Windows 7):

The actual request: "REQUEST_URI"=>"/se/sok?q=k\xC3\xB6k"
The first image that is requested: "HTTP_REFERER"=>"http://10.180.12.113:3000/se/sok?q=k\xC3\xB6k"

When I have already performed a search and then pressing enter in the address field. The address field contains "http://10.180.12.113:3000/se/sok?q=kök": "REQUEST_URI"=>"/se/sok?q=k\xF6k"

"\xC3\xB6" is Ruby's way of showing multibyte characters in ascii strings. In this case, the UTF-8 character is "ö". As you can see, none of the cases is URL encoded. Some cases (including IE10) sends data encoded as ISO-8859-1, that would be "\xF6".

In my App, the address bar contain `/produkte/suche?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=b%C3%A4ume` after the search in IE6 and IE10. Because it´s already escaped, it will not cause any problems when I press Enter in the address bar again. When I manually change the escaped character back to `bäume` in the address bar I got the same exception. But normal users won´t do that...

What do you mean with "The first image that is requested"? I don´t think it´s a good idea to rely on the referer for fetching images, because the browser can sent fake ones or no referer at all.

Did you manipulate the params of your form in any way? I have an other App where I have a POST form, strip out some of the params in the controller action and redirect the user to a different action with some of the params in the URI. I did a quick test with non UTF-8 characters (normally this in an admin area with predefined params from a select) and then I have to escape the strings manually with something like this: `new_params = "?" + striped_params.map{|k,v| "#{k}=#{URI.parser.escape(v)}" }.join('&')`

Beware, some browsers display I escaped in the bar but send escaped values. I believe Chrome does this, for example.

I mean after the first request the HTML is returned and the browser starts to do new request for assets (images, CSS JavaScript and so on).

> Did you manipulate the params of your form in any way?

No.

> Beware, some browsers display I escaped in the bar but send escaped values. I believe Chrome does this, for example.

Firefox and Chrome, possibly Safari as well, show URL's unescaped but sends the data escaped. But what I'm looking at is the data received in Rails.

Firefox and Chrome display the URI unescaped but when you copy it, it´s escaped. In Safari (OSX 10.8) the copied URI is unescaped.

I set up an TestApp to look if I could reproduce the issue. If someone´s interested I can share it on Github. 

First I run the App local:

I pasted the unescaped URI `/products/search?utf8=✓&q=bäume&commit=Search` into IE8 and IE10 and got a 400 - Bad Request and WebBrick logs:
[2013-03-29 18:26:13] ERROR bad URI `/products/search?utf8=?&q=b?ume&commit=Search'.

Then I cloned the App on my testserver which run with Apache and passenger. Here the result of pasting the unescaped URI is a ArgumentError - invalid byte sequence in UTF-8.

Maybe someone with a deeper insight in the Rails internals can say if this is a Rails issue and how to solve it.
We had similar problem with Apache and Passenger.

this is a problem w/ `request.fullpath` as well. In particular, we had an issue where a site was linking to a search result. In IE, the utf8 snowman came across as ASCII-8BIT in fullpath. We were rendering fullpath to the page as part of some tracking so it blew up. Forcing encoding on fullpath worked fine but it was a bear to track down.

The HTTP specs (RFC2616 via reference to RFC822) indicate that header values should be ASCII strings; sending anything else is not compliant. Neither is sending URIs that contain non-ASCII characters. It sounds like IE is the one falling down on the job here...

> The HTTP specs (RFC2616 via reference to RFC822) indicate that header values should be ASCII strings; sending anything else is not compliant. Neither is sending URIs that contain non-ASCII characters

Does that mean it's ok to send non-ASCII if it's escaped? Otherwise Rails breaking that itself by sending ✓, the check mark.

> It sounds like IE is the one falling down on the job here...

Surprise surprise, it's always IE :angry:.
Is there are any working solution to resolve this issue?
@dmitry do you have a specific problem or are you talking generally about the problem?

In our application we have around 20 exceptions per day (they are appearing in the two places) with following info:

`Encoding::CompatibilityError: incompatible character encodings: ASCII-8BIT and UTF-8`

As I've investigated yet, those exceptions risen only for the IE10 and IE11 (I guess, when client clicks the back button in the browser... still haven't enough time to reproduce it) and it happens with one of these request parameters:

```
request.original_fullpath # I guess only that one raises an exception
request.host # because this one returns an IP address
```

Those request parameters are concatenated with the UTF-8 string. 

Some of the issues happen previously that are also regarding the `incompatible character encodings` have been fixed with one of this gems:

https://github.com/whitequark/rack-utf8_sanitizer
https://github.com/singlebrook/utf8-cleaner
https://github.com/alext/invalid_utf8_rejector

But not all.

So I don't know, should the `ORIGINAL_FULLPATH` be also fixed using the `force_encoding` and `encoding` methods, like it does with the other `env` variables in the gems above. Or the issue with something else...

> Is there are any working solution to resolve this issue?

@dmitry We've been using a solution similar to the `encode` method I posted in the original issue.
